verifiedFacts.claim: Joni Mitchell said that “All I Want” has more tooth than most of her other early songs and that its meaning is plain-speak rather than hidden between the lines.

semanticReview.notes: Actual retained pages and snapshots, exact containment, SHA-256 reproduction, canonical URL/source identity, semantic scope, catalog identity, evidence borrowing, boilerplate, and unsupported-analysis checks passed.

sourceRefs.extract: I like the song. It's got more tooth than most of the other [early] songs. But I don't know what to say about it. It's funny how people keep looking between the lines of songs to see what is hidden there. Well, I'm not an evasive writer. You don't have to dig under the words for the meaning. The meaning is all there. It's very plain-speak.

sourceRefs.extract: The "Blue" tracks that are specifically about Nash - "My Old Man" and "River" - cover their relationship from opposite ends of the spectrum: On the former, Mitchell sings about a domestic bliss that doesn't "need no piece of paper," while the latter is a breakup lament about losing "the best baby that I ever had"."

verifiedFacts.claim: Joni Mitchell said that poverty forced her to give up her daughter for adoption, and identified Kilauren as the daughter she was singing about in “Little Green.”

semanticReview.notes: Actual retained pages and snapshots, exact containment, SHA-256 reproduction, canonical URL/source identity, semantic scope, catalog identity, evidence borrowing, boilerplate, and unsupported-analysis checks passed.

sourceRefs.extract: "All those songs I wrote the way I did because I had to," she explains. "I was emotionally disturbed, again, which brings out the poet in me. I had some hard life changes handed to me. The story is out on the streets now, but what happened was that I had to give up my daughter for adoption. Because of poverty. Not having the money to feed and clothe her and put a roof over her head." Kilauren is the daughter Joni was singing about in 'Little Green' from Blue.
